answer: The coefficient estimate (change in log-odds) for age is approximately -0.075 (log-odds per year; OR ≈ 0.928). In a simple logistic regression of camrelizumab treatment response (PR = responder vs PD/SD = non-responder) on age (n = 80, statsmodels Logit, converged), the age coefficient is -0.0750 (SE 0.0244, z = -3.08, p = 0.0021, 95% CI -0.123 to -0.027). Older patients have lower odds of response: each additional year of age multiplies the odds of response by ≈ 0.93. Note the data's perfect Group-Efficacy alignment (Group 1: all 41 PR; Group 2: 22 PD + 17 SD), so using Groups (1 vs 2) as the outcome yields the identical coefficient -0.0750. A sensitivity check with the alternative coding (PR/SD vs PD) gives -0.054, but the primary answer is -0.075.
